Great Local Eats
Mar 2017
We just knew it had to be good when all we saw were locals eating at this little corner spot just down a block from the Ben Thanh Market. We asked for a table for two, there weren't any available. But...no worries! The young woman who greeted us went to a closet and pulled out a table top that she set up and dragged over two stools and set us up just like that! We ordered the crab spring rolls, grilled pork both served with vermicelli and condiments plus the Cantonese fried rice. The menu has pictures so it's super easy for you to point out when ordering because staff spoke very little English. Utterly. And. Truly. Delicious.

Good Local Food in Busy Area.
Sep 2016 • Solo
I have been here a few times now over the years and have no complaints.
The food is authentically local and served in a no-frills local restaurant.
The food is more expensive than many other local eateries for sure... but in these ones you would be sitting on a plastic stool on the pavement. This restaurant is a step up from that!
Having said that, if you want air conditioning and white tablecloths you will pay more again.
I say this in many of my reviews... you get what you pay for!
And what you get here is good honest local food and efficient service.
The menu is easy to follow and has "daily specials" which I did not understand at first because I ordered the "Sunday special" on a friday and had the error of my ways explained to me... in a fashion.
I did then order the Friday dish of the day and enjoyed it very much..
To sum up... good local food, served quick and good value.

Late lunch
Jun 2016 • Solo
I ordered Bun Cha and a sugar cane juice. Came in just before 3pm which may be why the broth was only luke warm to cold. I don't know if I just misunderstand how this dish should be eaten but the vermicelli was also cold. There were plenty of herbs provided with this dish and I actually wish there was more vermicelli. The bean sprouts were also fresh. I didn't like the spots on the basil though however I enjoyed it. There was no way I could finish the lettuce and all the herbs. There was one herb I had not seen before, but didn't like.
The pork itself was very nice, juicy and tasty. I could have eaten more of that.
The sugar cane juice was excellent. 
Inexpensive lunch at 80k dong.

One of a few places that serve Bun Cha in HCMC
Dec 2015 • Family
This restaurant served bun cha, which I understand is not that common in the south of Vietnam, and since my daughter happened to express a craving for it (after enjoying it twice in Hanoi), we settled on Quan Hoa Dong.

There is an English menu provided and so we had no problem ordering. Prices seemed rather steep compared to those in Hanoi's Old Quarter (Bun cha here was VND 70k compared to 35-45k in Hanoi OQ), but then I have to consider the fact that this is smack in the tourist belt of HCMC, and that this was a proper sit-down eatery, not a side-walk stall!) Unlike Hanoi, the bun cha here only had strips of grilled meat and no pork patties/pork bellies, but then this happens to be somewhat more healthy as the meat is relatively lean.

Overall we were satisfied with the food and relative cleanliness of the place. But when we were paying the bill, we were initially told to pay VND420k (for 4 of us), and after expressing a bit of incredulity, it was "corrected" to 320k. Oh well, if there had been any "accidental" attempt to scam us, it would seem we ended up as the winners, for in my estimation, the bill should have been 340k!
